title: Convolution theorem for the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and let $f, g : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$, with convolution $(f * g)(x) = \mathbb{E}_y\!\left[f(y)\,g(x - y)\right]$ and Fourier coefficients $\hat{f}(s) = \langle f, \chi_s\rangle$ taken at any frequency $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then the Fourier transform carries convolution to pointwise multiplication:
\[
  \widehat{f * g}(s) = \hat{f}(s)\,\hat{g}(s).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f, g are complex-valued functions on Z_k^n
s is a frequency in Z_k^n
replaced:
For $f, g : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{C}$ and $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$,
\[
  \widehat{f * g}(s) = \hat{f}(s)\,\hat{g}(s).
\]
Convolution in the spatial domain corresponds to pointwise multiplication in
the frequency domain.
